rationale: lendzy.co.uk is one of the five register-less finance sites named in RFC_060 section 1: it has ZERO evidence_base rows [MEASURED 2026-09-02], so its numeric scan never arms and its daily citation refresh passes over an empty set — a clean run that means nothing. RFC_060 section 4 says populating these registers is content work, needs no RFC, and is the single highest-value action arising from that RFC. The owner's instruction on 2026-09-02 was to make lendzy's retracted claim ('checked against the FCA handbook, rule by rule' — the phrase that became bugs_closed/414) TRUE rather than merely deleted, with a local mirror and live re-checking. This migration delivers the live-re-checking half outright and with no code: the existing daily refresher (refresh_evidence_base_action.go + evidence_citations.go, CLM-007/008) re-fetches every citation URL and re-checks its verbatim quote, so the eight facts start being verified against the live handbook the moment the row exists. Every quote was verified through the PRODUCTION matcher before being written — cmd/fcaquotecheck calls datahelpers.VisibleTextFromHTML and datahelpers.QuoteFoundInText, the exact functions the refresher calls, not a re-implementation — and all eight returned true with a deliberately-absent control returning false in the same run. Checking each rule the site cites against the handbook text also found two WRONG attributions in live copy, recorded here in the register (with the correct rule) but deliberately NOT fixed in the served pages, because rewriting published prose on an automated finding is authority the owner withheld (bugs_open/320 section 15).

plan.summary: ROUND 2, answering all round-1 objections. (a) The lossy-round-trip HIGH: real hazard, and its own landmine text answers it — the typed structs are lossy and FOR THAT REASON both live writers deliberately work on map[string]interface{} (refresh_evidence_base_action.go:683, evidence_citations.go:350), so the daily refresher does not delete rule/corrects_site_citation. Because a FUTURE writer could round-trip through the struct, the two corrections are now ALSO recorded outside the round-trip surface: a doc_notes row written by the migration (verified in the DO/RAISE block), plus site_specs.notes (a real column), plus lane NOTES and migration 696. (b) pinned: declared NON-load-bearing (write_site_spec drops it); kept as convention only. (c) The truncated site_id was sketch shorthand — the committed file carries the full UUID throughout; a new guard resolves the id against sites and aborts unless it names lendzy.co.uk. (d) Dispatch NAMED AND MEASURED: scheduled task evidence-freshness, enabled, 86400s, last_triggered_at 2026-09-02 09:08:57Z; site selection is fleet-wide by aspect (refresh_evidence_base_action.go:278), no per-site registration — lendzy is reached on the first daily tick after the row exists. (e) Compliance urgency: OVERTAKEN same day — the owner ruled 'please fix both'; migration 696 (committed, corr bb352ee8) fixes every storage layer incl. the content_direction spec and the loancash fork and files 11 rerenders; apply sequenced after the announced chassis roll. (f) The rule-renumbering standing gap stays named; its closer is the rule-span checker (RFC_060 3d/Q6), owner-approved to build 2026-09-02. Everything else unchanged from round 1.
plan.risks: (1) A quote that does not match what the refresher extracts is classified citation_lost — drift — every day for ever, and that false alarm is indistinguishable from a real one. Mitigated by verifying all eight through the production functions with a negative control, not by inspection. (2) handbook.fca.org.uk returns HTTP 200 for EVERY path including invented rules (LANDMINES entry, same date), so status is worthless as an existence test; all eight URLs were confirmed by <title>. (3) STRUCTURAL LIMIT, stated rather than hidden: the Handbook has no rule-level URL. CONC 6.7 is 54 rules on one page carrying both 6.7.17 and 6.7.23, so the refresher keeps the QUOTES honest but cannot keep the `rule` field honest — a quote from one rule verifies against a citation naming its neighbour. `rule` is therefore a human-verified field, checked by hand on 2026-09-02, and the gap is filed as RFC_060 section 3d / Q6 by the claims-verification lane with a fix sketch. (4) idx_site_specs_current is UNIQUE on (site_id, aspect) WHERE is_current, so a register written by another session in the interval would collide; the guard aborts on any existing row rather than superseding work unseen. (5) Pacing: eight facts sharing five URLs are re-fetched daily by an unthrottled fetchCitationDocument (one request per fact, no dedup). Eight is small against the fleet's 39 citation facts, but the lane's ratchet line records that pacing must land before any bulk mirror scales this up, and that pacing is a change to a shared fetch path and therefore register/RFC material, not a lane patch.

edits.rationale: The register. A DO/RAISE guard refusing to run if any evidence_base row already exists for the site, one INSERT of the eight-fact JSON, and a DO/RAISE verify asserting 8 facts, 8 with an FCA handbook URL and a substantive quote, 8 naming a CONC/DISP rule, and exactly 2 recording a corrected site citation. Verification is DO/RAISE throughout because a verify block of bare SELECTs cannot stop the COMMIT.

Deletes the register, guarded so it refuses unless exactly one unmodified 695-authored row with 8 facts is present — because the daily refresher WRITES to this row (bumping accessed dates and classifying drift), so a blind delete would discard its work too, not only ours. The header states what rolling back costs: lendzy returns to a vacuously-clean daily run, and the record of the two wrong live citations survives only in lane prose, nowhere a machine reads.
